Analyzes John's absence from the 1636 Weymouth property grants as the beginning of the plausible arrival range.
Uses the completed Boston record-class sweep as part of the assessment of an earlier arrival.
Explains why 1636 begins the plausible arrival range and why 1638–40 is the best estimate.

shortLabel: Why the arrival range begins in 1636
statement: John was not among the men receiving Weymouth property grants in 1636. Earlier Massachusetts arrivals are more likely to leave records, and the early population was small. The well-preserved Boston records also contain no John Gurney of his generation. Taken together, those facts make an arrival before 1636 extremely unlikely. They support 1636 as the beginning of the plausible range and 1638–40 as the best estimate.
